Question B-001-016-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Fast-scan television on 145 MHz is prohibited because 145 MHz is in the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band with a 30 kHz maximum. Fast-scan amateur television (ATV) needs more bandwidth than that limit allows.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "FT8 on 14.074 MHz": Franke-Taylor 8-frequency-shift keying (FSK) (FT8) is a narrow digital mode, so many contacts fit inside one single-sideband (SSB) voice signal. It is not the wide-signal problem.
- sourceIndex 2: "Morse radiotelegraphy (CW) on 10.145 MHz": Continuous wave (CW) is narrow and fits the 10.145 MHz narrow-band context. As a width comparison, CW is narrower than SSB, which is narrower than frequency modulation (FM).
- sourceIndex 3: "Fast-scan television (ATV) on 440 MHz": 440 MHz is outside the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band with the 30 kHz limit, while the bandwidth conflict is fast-scan ATV at 145 MHz.
